title: We are trying to raise a Series A round of €2.8 million from a Vienna-based impact fund but our three-year financial projections have been rejected twice because the reviewers say our unit-economics model is not structured to institutional investor standards.

record.text: We are trying to raise a Series A round of €2.8 million from a Vienna-based impact fund but our three-year financial projections have been rejected twice because the reviewers say our unit-economics model is not structured to institutional investor standards.
record.detail: We are in discussions with Waldviertel Impact Ventures, a Vienna-based fund, about a Series A round of €2.8 million. The money would go toward expanding our municipal sales team, funding firmware development for a next-generation device and covering a planned move to a larger assembly facility. We submitted a full financial package twice. Both times the fund's analyst returned it saying our unit-economics presentation does not meet the structure they require — specifically, they want a clear separation of hardware margin, subscription gross margin and professional services margin, along with cohort-based customer lifetime value calculations for both the tour operator and municipality segments, and a sensitivity table for three hardware volume scenarios. Our current financial model is an Excel workbook our office manager built over the years. It tracks overall revenue and costs accurately but mixes the revenue streams together and was not designed to answer the specific questions institutional investors ask. We have a part-time bookkeeper and a tax accountant who visits quarterly; neither has experience structuring investment-grade materials. The fund has indicated they will review a third submission if we resubmit before the end of Q1 2025.
